articleHeadline: Namibia suspends beef exports due to outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease.
articleSummary: Namibia suspended beef and sheep meat exports after the first outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) in the southern livestock belt in six decades. Government spokesperson Romeo Muyunda told AFP that this is the country’s first epidemic since independence in 1990 and will hit the sector. FMD is a highly contagious viral disease not dangerous to humans but virulent in cattle, sheep and goats, causing fever, blisters and sometimes death. The outbreak breached a sanitary cordon that separates the endemic north from the south, marking the first spread to the southern region since 1964; Namibia borders Angola to the north. Namibia is the eighth Southern African country affected by FMD this year, following Botswana, Lesotho, Mozambique, South Africa, Zambia and Zimbabwe. In 2025 Namibia exported over 13,000 tonnes of beef, more than 90% to Europe. Meatco says it will review transit shipments; no recalls announced yet.
